title: Lexicon — Conlang Workbench
description: Pick a language's sounds and syllables, run a stack of sound changes over it, and export the dictionary it leaves behind.
concept: A workbench for inventing a language the way a historical linguist would reconstruct one. You choose a phoneme inventory from an IPA grid, weight the syllable templates, then write ordered sound-change rules in real notation (p > f / V_V) that sweep across every word at once. A 56-word lexicon, six affixes, a word order and a set of interlinear example phrases all regenerate live, and every headword can be opened to watch its proto-form fall through the changes one law at a time.
features: IPA inventory grid where each sound cycles unused → in → frequent (3× weight)
Weighted syllable templates over seven phoneme classes (C V P N S L G) plus word-length distribution
Ordered sound-change engine with real rule notation, environments, deletion, reordering and per-rule on/off
Per-entry derivation drawer showing proto-form → each law that fired → written form
Editable romanisation for exactly the sounds that survive the changes
Generated grammar sketch: six affixes, three word orders, six interlinear glossed phrases
Lock individual roots so rerolling the lexicon keeps them
Export the dictionary as .md, .json or .csv, copy the IPA list, and share the whole language as a URL
Five starting languages and localStorage autosave
tech: Rule-based sound-change engine with simultaneous application

interaction.mouse: Tap sounds in the IPA grid to cycle them in and out; drag the weight sliders for syllable shapes and word length.
interaction.click: Click a headword to open its derivation; click the ring to lock a root against rerolls; toggle any sound change on or off.
interaction.touch: Everything is tap-driven; the tab bar scrolls horizontally and the dictionary sits below the controls on narrow screens.
interaction.keyboard: 1–5 switch tabs, r rerolls the unlocked words, n draws a new seed; Enter submits a new syllable shape or rule.
